rationale:
bugs_open/083's council round (corr 05a3d1c8, APPROVED) left one named open residual: the guardian seat's point that the detected-item-promoter's doors hold rows silently, so a pipeline value that stops being promotable produces no signal beyond a pile that looks like normal backlog. The bug file records the seat's suggested cheap control verbatim: 'have the pre_query return a third column counting detected rows a door held, so the scheduler's own log makes it visible.'

That remedy is INOPERATIVE as stated, and measuring it is what this change is really about. Measured at the running service on 2026-08-17: every tick of this task emits one line carrying no numbers at all — {"caller":"scheduler/main.go:274","msg":"Pre-query task completed (no message fired)","task":"detected-item-promoter"} — six such lines in --tail=3000. For a fire_message=false task the pre_query result is merged into inputData and then discarded unlogged, so `promoted` and `pairs` have never been readable either. A third column would have been write-only.

So the fix is in two halves. The framework half is one change in cmd/scheduler/main.go so EVERY CTE-only scheduled task logs its own pre_query result — this is SCH-006's observability gap, not a promoter-specific one, and eight tasks share it. The instance half is migration 458, which supplies the numbers worth logging and corrects a second defect found while writing it: the final SELECT's `WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM promoted) > 0` does not suppress anything (aggregate-only target list, no GROUP BY, so one row returns regardless), which means the task claims its `maintenance` concurrency slot on every idle tick and defeats bugs_open/048's release-on-no-op fix.

The held count is NOT computed by writing the door predicates a second time. That rule has changed twice in one day (444 added the pipeline allow-list and the success floor; 454 corrected both to count `verified`), so a mirrored copy would have drifted within four hours — the idx_swi_dedup/workItemTerminalStatuses lockstep trap in a new place. Instead the predicates move into a `scored` CTE evaluated once per row, of which `candidates` and `held` are complementary halves by construction.

What the change reveals on the day it ships is the argument for it: held = 2, and one of them is 444's own success floor holding a live row for the first time (literal_markdown -> page-build-handler). 444 recorded both doors as holding zero rows at apply and called them 'doors, not repairs'. One is now load-bearing and nothing can see it.

plan.summary: bugs_open/083's promoter holds rows silently: its doors refuse work with no signal, and the scheduler never logs a CTE-only task's pre_query result at all, so `promoted`/`pairs` have never been readable either and the residual's stated remedy (add a third column) would have been write-only. This changes cmd/scheduler/main.go so EVERY CTE-only scheduled task logs its own result (the framework half, SCH-006's observability gap), and migration 458 supplies the held count plus a reason per held pair, restructuring the candidates CTE so each door is evaluated once and `candidates`/`held` are complementary halves rather than two copies of a rule that has already changed twice today. 458 also corrects a non-suppressing WHERE that made the task claim its maintenance concurrency slot on every idle tick, defeating bugs_open/048's release-on-no-op.

edits.rationale: The framework half. For a fire_message=false task the pre_query IS the worker, and its result was computed, merged and then discarded — so a task that promoted 20 rows and one that promoted none emit the identical log line. Logging the result makes every CTE-only scheduled task (8 of them today) report its own work. dynamicData is currently scoped inside the pre-query block, so it is hoisted to be readable at the CTE-only exit.
edits.sketch:
@@ inputData := task.InputData
+		// Kept past the merge so the CTE-only branch below can report what the
+		// query actually did — for fire_message=false tasks the merged
+		// input_data is never sent anywhere, so this is the only surviving
+		// evidence of the tick's work.
+		var preQueryResult json.RawMessage
 		if task.PreQuery.Valid && task.PreQuery.String != "" {
@@
+			preQueryResult = dynamicData
 			inputData, err = mergeJSON(task.InputData, dynamicData)
@@ if !task.FireMessage {
 			logger.Info("Pre-query task completed (no message fired)",
-				zap.String("task", task.Name))
+				zap.String("task", task.Name),
+				zap.ByteString("pre_query_result", truncateForLog(preQueryResult, preQueryLogLimit)))

edits.rationale: A pre_query may return an unbounded string_agg and one pathological row should not dominate the log. The cap ANNOUNCES itself: a truncation that hides itself would let a partial reading pass as a whole one, which is the same defect class the logging above exists to close, so it must not be reintroduced by the fix.
Pins the CAP rather than the logging: the assertion is that a cut result carries the marker and an uncut one does NOT. A silent truncation is the failure mode worth a test here.

Supplies the numbers. Restructures the candidates CTE so every door is evaluated ONCE per row in a `scored` CTE, of which `candidates` and `held` are complementary halves — deliberately NOT a second negated copy of the predicates, which would have drifted (444 -> 454 changed them within four hours). Also fixes the non-suppressing WHERE. Guarded on a verbatim pre-image md5 so that a concurrent edit by the still-open 277 lane makes it ABORT rather than silently revert that lane's work. 430/444/454 are ledger-recorded and are not edited.
edits.sketch:
DO $$ BEGIN
  IF live_md5 <> '1d1efee2913929db7b6b5395d8421ecc' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION '458: ABORTING — the live pre_query is not the text this migration was written against ...';
  END IF; END $$;

UPDATE scheduled_tasks SET pre_query = $Q$
  WITH scored AS (SELECT wi.id, wi.item_type, wi.handler_agent, wi.created_at,
         (wi.pipeline IN ('build','content','design')) AS pipe_ok,
         EXISTS (...agent_definitions...) AS handler_ok,
         EXISTS (...status IN ('complete','verified')...) AS known_good,
         (SELECT (c+f) < 5 OR c >= 0.25*(c+f) FROM (...) hist) AS floor_ok
       FROM site_work_items wi
       WHERE wi.status='detected' AND COALESCE(wi.handler_agent,'') <> ''),
  candidates AS (SELECT id FROM scored WHERE pipe_ok AND handler_ok AND known_good AND floor_ok ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 20),
  held AS (SELECT item_type, handler_agent,
             CASE WHEN NOT handler_ok THEN 'handler not a live agent'
                  WHEN NOT pipe_ok THEN 'pipeline not in allow-list'
                  WHEN NOT known_good THEN 'pair has never completed one (awaiting a hand canary)'
                  ELSE 'pair below the 25% success floor' END AS reason
           FROM scored WHERE NOT (pipe_ok AND handler_ok AND known_good AND floor_ok)),
  promoted AS (UPDATE site_work_items ... RETURNING ...)
  SELECT COUNT(*)::text AS promoted, string_agg(...) AS pairs,
         (SELECT COUNT(*)::text FROM held) AS held,
         (SELECT string_agg(... || ' (' || reason || ')', '; ') FROM held) AS held_detail
  FROM promoted
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 OR (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM held) > 0
$Q$ WHERE name='detected-item-promoter';

edits.rationale: Separate rollback file alongside a separate verify block, as the needle-gate discipline asks and as 444's round required. It restores the pre-image byte-exactly and ASSERTS that it did; it also refuses if the live text is neither 458's output nor the pre-image, because that means a third edit landed and blind restoration would revert it.

grounded_in: bugs_open/083: 'The seat's real point is the *silent* failure mode — a new pipeline value stops being promotable with no signal beyond a growing pile that looks like normal backlog. That is a live residual and it is sharper than my risk 4 admitted... The cheap control, when someone takes it: have the pre_query return a third column counting `detected` rows a door held, so the scheduler's own log makes it visible.'

cmd/scheduler/main.go:268-277 (the fire_message=false exit): the ONLY field on the line is zap.String("task", task.Name). The merged inputData is never logged and, because fireTrigger is not reached, never sent anywhere either — so for a CTE-only task the pre_query result has no consumer at all.

Measured live 2026-08-17: `kubectl -n ai-persona-system logs -l app=kafka-scheduler --tail=3000 | grep detected-item-promoter` returns 6 identical 'Pre-query task completed (no message fired)' lines and no counts.

Row-suppression proven read-only against an empty CTE: `... FROM promoted WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM promoted) > 0` returns one row ('0', NULL); the HAVING form returns 0 rows. So the dynamicData==nil branch at cmd/scheduler/main.go:200-216 is unreachable for this task and the slot claim at :264-266 always happens.

cmd/scheduler/main.go:200-216 stamps BOTH timestamps on the zero-row path and logs 'Pre-query found no rows — task ran with nothing to do' (introduced by dc2e4b61a for bugs_open/048). This refutes concept-register SCH-007's claim that a pre_query must return at least one row or the timestamps never advance; that entry is corrected in this change.

Held set measured live before applying: literal_markdown->page-build-handler (1 row, below the 25% floor) and placeholder_contact->page-build-handler (1 row, pair has never completed one). Migration 444's own verify block asserted both doors held ZERO rows at apply on 2026-08-17.

Concurrency: detected-item-promoter is in concurrency_group='maintenance' with max_concurrent=1 alongside database-cleanup, feasibility-recheck, stale-work-item-reaper and work-item-archiver. Measured the same day, NO group-mate is starved (all within 1.04 intervals of due) — so the suppression fix is a door, not a repair, and is submitted as such.
plan.risks: (1) The logged pre_query result is whatever the task author SELECTed. A task that selected a secret would now log it. Today's eight CTE-only tasks select counts, ids and reasons only; the code comment says so at the log site. Stated rather than mitigated, because the alternative (an allow-list of column names) would silently drop the diagnostic a future author adds. (2) The suppression changes when the task claims its concurrency slot. Measured: no maintenance group-mate is starved today, so this is a door, not a repair — but it does mean an idle promoter tick now takes the 'found no rows' branch, which stamps both timestamps and releases the slot. That is bugs_open/048's intended behaviour, not new behaviour. (3) The held count and held_detail columns are inert until kafka-scheduler is rebuilt and rolled. Applying 458 before the roll is safe and observable only through the suppression. The Go half must be verified at the artefact after the roll, not assumed from the commit. (4) 458's positive control asserts held >= 1. If the held set is ever legitimately empty when someone re-applies this file, the migration will refuse. That is deliberate — a counter nobody has shown can count is not evidence — but a future re-applier must read the control rather than delete it. (5) The `scored` restructure is asserted behaviour-identical on the promotable set by a same-transaction negative control (old predicate count == new predicate count). That check compares counts, not row identity; two sets of equal size but different membership would pass. Judged acceptable because the predicates are textually the same expressions moved, not rewritten.
